item.title: The Gemini-Powered Google Home Speaker Is Finally Here
item.description: Arriving six years after Google’s last smart speaker, the new HomePod-style device was redesigned to play host to Gemini’s chatbot.

item.title: ‘Dangerous’ AI Models Are Coming No Matter What
item.description: The US government crackdown on Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 hides a glaring truth: AI models with advanced hacking capabilities will soon be the norm.

item.title: My Father Wants to Age in Place. AI Will Be Watching
item.description: Devices that monitor seniors for safety are appealing to worried loved ones and underresourced home care agencies.

item.title: What Do We Need From Our Homes Right Now?
item.description: The global editorial directors of WIRED and Architectural Digest on teaming up to help you understand how we live today, and what comes next.

item.title: ‘Pretty Crazy’ Token Usage Is Testing Bosses’ Bet on AI
item.description: A Silicon Valley software maker and an ecommerce company reveal to WIRED how they are navigating the emerging challenge of “tokenomics.”

item.title: DOJ Lawyers Argue xAI Is ‘Vital’ for National Security in NAACP Lawsuit
item.description: In a bid to dismiss a lawsuit over xAI’s polluting gas turbines, the Justice Department claimed the company is integral to military operations—including the Iran War.

item.title: Anthropic Is Still at Odds With the White House Over Claude Fable 5
item.description: Anthropic leaders flew to Washington, DC, to meet with White House officials on Monday. After high-level talks, they’re still split on the risk Claude Fable 5 presents.

item.title: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth Admits the Company’s AI Reorg Was ‘Atrocious’
item.description: In an internal memo seen by WIRED, Bosworth promised employees more stability, better communication, and the return of workplace perks as the company seeks to improve morale.

item.title: Meta Tapped a Pentagon Supplier to Prototype Face Recognition for Its Glasses
item.description: Rank One, whose board includes a former CIA deputy director and a former FBI science chief, supplied face recognition to Meta for internal development of its smart glasses app.

item.title: A Court Has Ruled That Google Is Liable for False Statements Generated by AI Overviews
item.description: The ruling holds that a company that designs, trains, operates, and manages an AI system must assume legal liability for any damages caused by the responses it generates.
